predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: Bosnia, 'part of Byzantium from 1167 to 1180' with nominal rule (Banate page), freed by Ban Kulin after Manuel I's death in 1180

successors.name: Kingdom of Bosnia
successors.text: Cliopatria's Banate shape of 1375-1384, which is the kingdom Tvrtko I crowned in 1377

ledger.x: 1180: Ban Kulin frees Bosnia from Byzantium when Manuel I dies.
1241: the Tatars kill Coloman at Mohi and Ninoslav retakes most of Bosnia.
1299: the Subic of Bribir take the banate.
1322: Stephen II defeats Mladen II Subic.
1324: Stephen II incorporates Usora and Soli.

c. 1326: Stephen II takes the Zavrsje region. Livno, Duvno, Glamoc and the nearby poljes, 'just before the Hum conquest'; the date is approximate and the page names no holder. Reopened: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zavr%C5%A1je is only a disambiguation page of villages and says nothing on Livno, Duvno or Glamoc; no…
1326: Stephen II conquers Zahumlje (Hum) from the Serbian vassals.
1329: Stephen II adds Nevesinje and Zagorje after fighting Dusan at Priboj.
1357: Tvrtko gives Donji Kraji, western Hum and Drijeva to Louis I of Hungary as Elizabeth's dowry.
1363: Louis I of Hungary invades Bosnia.

March 1366: the contest over Donji Kraji and Usora ends when Tvrtko, who had fled to Louis's court after the magnates' revolt of February 1366, returns 'in March' with Louis's likely military aid ('provided Tvrtko with aid (likely military)') and 'reestablished control over a part of the country... including Donji…
March 1366: Tvrtko returns from exile and regains Donji Kraji, Rama and Hum.
1373: Tvrtko defeats Nicholas Altomanovic and takes upper Podrinje, Gacko and part of Polimlje.
Early 1377: Tvrtko takes Trebinje, Konavli and Dracevica 'with Travunian help'; the extract names no previous holder (Altomanovic's former lands), so the counterpart is left as nobody.
1377: Tvrtko I is crowned king, ending the banate.

wars.name: Hungarian crusade against Bosnia
wars.outcome: Coloman of Hungary, ban from 1235, holds most of Bosnia until his death at Mohi in 1241; Ninoslav retreats to Dubrovnik in 1240 and restores control over most of Bosnia in 1241.

wars.name: Subic hold on Bosnia and the Battle of Skradin
wars.outcome: The Subic of Bribir hold the banate from 1299; Stephen II defeats Mladen II near Skradin in 1322 and rules in fact from then.

wars.name: Bosnian-Serbian war over Hum
wars.outcome: Stephen II conquers Zahumlje in 1326 and adds Nevesinje and Zagorje in 1329 after fighting Dusan at Priboj.

wars.name: Serbian invasion of Bosnia under Dusan
wars.outcome: Stephen raids Konavli and the Bay of Kotor in 1349; Dusan invades in October 1350; 'Ban Stephen II therefore won the war, even though he lost most of the battles'.

wars.name: Tvrtko against Nicholas Altomanovic
wars.outcome: Tvrtko takes upper Podrinje, Gacko and part of Polimlje in the autumn of 1373.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian war (Stephen II)
wars.outcome: Stephen seeks a Venetian alliance in 1343 and is nicknamed 'Devil's Student' for passing Hungarian positions to the Venetians; no border change.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Bosnia (Louis I)
wars.outcome: Louis I attacks Donji Kraji in spring 1363 and a month later the Palatine Nicholas Kont strikes Usora; Vlatko Vukoslavic surrenders Kljuc, but Soko Grad and Srebrenik hold and the Hungarians withdraw ('Tvrtko's first victory against the Hungarian king'); the…

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines survive in the pages opened: the banate's marches (Usora and Soli, Hum, Donji Kraji, Podrinje) are approximate throughout.
